thread:
marta: quick sync  we need a pragmatic decision on local controlplane endpoints vs shared regional relays for private customers. i want a minimal operator surface and clear migration semantics.

ken: is this primarily about preserving egress identity (src-ip/cert SAN) or about reducing latency? we should call out priorities.

marta: both, but priority order: 1) safety (no secret leakage), 2) predictable identity for customers who audit, 3) operational cost.

oliver: other constraint: some customers require no inbound routes from operator side into their VPC. ENI approach needs cross-account role + delegated attachments which they sometimes disallow.

hana: options sketch:
- ENI-local: operator creates per-tenant ENI in customer VPC. gives stable src-ip and local DNS. higher cost, requires attachment privileges.
- Shared-regional-relay: operator routes tenant traffic through regional relays with operator-kept ENIs. cheaper but changes src-ip and may require proxying identity.
- Hybrid: attempt ENI first; if attachment blocked, fall back to relay with explicit customer opt-in.

marta: auth pattern proposals:
A) header-forwarding: preserve tenant identity in signed headers across relay. quick but audited customers object.
B) proxy-cert mint: operator mints ephemeral certs bound to tenant SAN, used by relay so apps see expected SANs. better audit trail but requires CA ops and short TTL.

ken: B preferred. need threat model: what if relay is compromised? ephemeral certs should be scoped and have narrow validity and revocation hooks.

oliver: revocation is tricky; but we can rotate an operator-signed intermediate per region used ONLY for relays. revoke intermediate if compromise—this is heavy. maybe prefer short TTL + rotation + anomaly alerts.

hana: footprint + billing: ENI-local adds a monthly charge per tenancy per region. recommend default=relay, opt-in=ENI-local for tenants with egress-ACls requirement. also add "preserve_identity" flag controlling proxy-cert vs header-forward.

marta: runtime cutover flow (hybrid):
1) operator attempts to provision ENI; if granted, create local endpoint and mirror minimal state read-only.
2) agent opens dual controlplane sessions: global + local (local read-only). verify local probe x3.
3) if probe passes and tenant config allows, flip DNS to local endpoint. agents keep dual sessions for ttl.
4) if ENI provisioning fails or tenant disallows, configure relay path with proxy-cert mode and register the relay as authorized egress for tenant.
5) on failover from ENI->relay, operator mints ephemeral proxy-cert and notifies tenant (emit metric).

ken: node identity & secret handling: never copy long-lived private keys into tenant VPC. local endpoints request short-lived tokens from global controlplane and sign CSRs locally. all long-term secrets stay in operator KMS.

oliver: RBAC rules: local endpoints are strictly read-only for mutating objects. any mutation request from local endpoint proxied to global and requires a signed attestation. helps avoid split-brain writes.

hana: metrics and signals: enis_provision_attempts, enis_provision_failures, cutover_success, fallback_to_relay_count, proxy_cert_issuance, srcip_delta_events. logs must include tenant id + attempt id for audits.

marta: rollout plan: canary with 1% tenants on relay-proxy-cert mode for two weeks; then invite 3 enterprise tenants to opt into ENI-local alpha. document limitations: fallback will change src-ip, proxy-cert TTL defaults = 5m, revocation = operator-initiated.

ops-bot: scheduled: canary/controlplane-handoff -> 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC

ken: ill draft the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, the hybrid config schema, and the ops playbook. tagging @marta @oliver for review. :+1:
